edits.Zeryab Estates is a private luxury retre: Zeryab Estates is a private luxury retreat in the heart of Marrakech, a city where centuries of Andalusian, Berber and Arab culture meet in something singular. The brief called for an identity that could carry all of that weight without collapsing under it.
edits.The property is defined by its relations: The property is defined by its relationship with time: ancient craft traditions, living architecture and a landscape that has resisted change. The brand had to speak to a discerning international audience while staying rooted in its place, not as nostalgia but as living continuity.
edits.Heritage and nature frame every experien: Heritage and nature frame every experience at Zeryab: palm-shaded courtyards, Moorish arches reflected in still water, the scent of aged cedar and orange blossom. The identity had to translate this sensory world into a mark that moves across every material with the same quiet authority.
edits.Marrakech · Moorish Heritage — Zeryab Es: Marrakech · The Moorish heritage behind Zeryab Estates
edits.The logomark draws from two of Morocco's: The logomark draws on two of Morocco's most enduring visual traditions: the pointed Moorish arch and the interlocking geometry of zellige tilework. Both follow the same logic, infinite complexity generated from a single precise rule. The arch frames space; the zellige fills it. Together they define the visual language of Moroccan sacred and domestic architecture.
edits.The mark abstracts these references into: The mark abstracts both into a single geometric emblem: an arch outline that, on closer inspection, holds a zellige-derived interlocking pattern at its core. It reads at once as place without resorting to ornamental cliché. It is architectural rather than decorative, structured rather than nostalgic.
edits.Typography was equally deliberate. Exten: Typography was just as deliberate. Extensive exploration of weight, spacing and proportion led to a custom-spaced wordmark that balances the geometric rigour of the mark with an open, breathing quality. The letters feel carved rather than printed: solid enough for embossing, refined enough for fine stationery.

edits.Typography Explorations — Custom Wordmar: Typography explorations · Developing the custom wordmark
edits.The final identity system is built aroun: The identity system is built around the architectural logomark, a clean geometric form that holds its own at any scale, from embossed collateral to signage, from a wax seal to a favicon. The ZERYAB ESTATES wordmark is set in wide-tracked capitals with custom spacing that gives the name the presence of an inscription.
edits.Six brand colors extracted directly from: The palette takes six colours from the Marrakech landscape: deep navy, dark umber, olive gold, sand tan, deep terracotta and burnt red. It feels both timeless and specific to its place. These are not decorative choices but materials translated into colour: the charcoal of hammered iron, the warmth of hand-pressed clay, the oxidised gold of ageing copper.
The system was designed for permanence. Every decision was tested on the materials it would live on: heavily textured papers, metallic foils, raw clay, woven textiles. It performs equally well at both extremes of luxury hospitality, from the intimacy of a guest welcome card to the authority of a façade plaque.
edits.Each color in the system was chosen for: Each colour was chosen for its resonance with the physical world of Marrakech: the deep navy of tile shadow, the umber of cedarwood grain, the gold of polished brass lanterns, the tan of sun-dried clay, the terracotta of handmade brick, the burnt red of poured iron. The palette holds together across print and screen, in daylight and by candlelight.
edits.Typography bridges the historical and th: Typography bridges the historic and the contemporary. Display text is set in elegantly spaced capitals with fine optical adjustments, a voice that belongs as much in a riad guestbook as in a contemporary art catalogue. Body text stays restrained and readable, giving the display work room to breathe.

edits.The application system spans stationery,: The applications span stationery, welcome collateral, amenities, textiles and architectural signage. Each surface called for its own reading of the mark, at times reduced to a single embossed letterform, at times expanded into an environmental graphic that fills a whole wall.
